title: A passed gate is not learning
statement: A lesson that passes every check is well formed, and a first-try answer shows the moment; whether anyone learned needs a later test on new items.
detail:
The reading project's quality gate certifies form, not outcome, by construction
(`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0069-self-audit-insights.qmd`); its engine's README says passing tests
proves plumbing, not learning (`grade3-reading/engine/README.md`); and a rise in completion alone was ruled
insufficient (`grade3-reading/artifacts/GOAL_grade3_hootl_convergence_2026_06_15.md`). First-try answers show the
moment: on a final test 5 minutes later restudying won, but after 2 days and a week prior testing gave much greater
retention (Roediger & Karpicke 2006, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x).
against:

### G5-POL-PRA-008: Reserve durable-mastery claims for a different-day, feedback-free assessment on novel items at or above eighty percent.
Acquisition, durable mastery, and transfer are different claims.
an acquisition checkpoint requires a substantial set of distinct, certified, feedback-free items, including integrative work, at the declared high-accuracy threshold;
durable mastery requires a different-day, feedback-free check on novel forms; and
transfer requires cold passages on never-taught topics and remains separate from course mastery or an impact claim.
